aggressive_definition: Advanced prostate cancer, defined as SEER stages three and four.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Cox proportional hazards regression was used to calculate hazard ratios (HR) of total and advanced (SEER states three and four; n = 54) prostate cancer and 95% confidence intervals (CI) adjusted for age, BMI at age 21, and intake of energy, saturated fat, and tomato products.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: In 1989, 3,892 men 35+ years old, who participated in CLUE II study of Washington County, MD, completed an abbreviated Block food frequency questionnaire.
reason: This prospective cohort assessed incident total prostate cancer and incident advanced prostate cancer defined as SEER stages three and four. The abstract reports total-disease estimates but no exposure-specific advanced-disease effect sizes.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: However, processed meat consumption was associated with a non-statistically significant higher risk of total (5+ vs. < or =1 servings/week: HR = 2.24; 95% CI 0.90-5.59) prostate cancer.
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate explicitly concerns total prostate cancer.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: There was no association across tertiles of dairy or calcium with total prostate cancer, although compared tp < or =1 servings/week consumption of 5+ servings/week of dairy foods was associated with an increased risk of prostate cancer (HR = 1.65, 98% CI 1.02-2.66).
estimate_classifications.reason: The dairy estimate is presented in the discussion of total prostate cancer and is not identified as an advanced-disease estimate.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Intakes of total mean (HR = 0.90, 95% CI 0.60-1.33, comparing highest to lowest tertile) and red meat (HR = 0.87, 95% CI 0.59-1.32) were not statistically significantly associated with prostate cancer.
estimate_classifications.reason: This red-meat estimate concerns prostate cancer overall and is not labeled as advanced.

additional_estimates.comparison: Not reported in the abstract for advanced prostate cancer
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: Intake of meat and dairy related foods was calculated using consumption frequency and portion size. Incident prostate cancer cases (n = 199) were ascertained through October 2004. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to calculate hazard ratios (HR) of total and advanced (SEER states three and four; n = 54) prostate cancer and 95% confidence intervals (CI) adjusted for age, BMI at age 21, and intake of energy, saturated fat, and tomato products.
